text:
Alex: heads up — after yesterday's scheduler change we see a regression in end-to-end p95 for chat with cached prefixes. digging into profiler now, but high level: continuous batching seems to interleave many short sessions which prevents KV warmstart locality 
Maria: ugh, saw p95 bump on dashboards too. what's the hit-rate delta?
Alex: cluster-level prefix cache hit_rate dropped from ~0.62 to ~0.18 on the affected pool after rollout. key entropy looks higher. snippet from the cache stats: 
```
pool: gpu-pool-7
prefix_cache: {hits: 18234, misses: 81900, hit_rate: 0.182}
continuous_batcher: {avg_batch_size: 5.1, avg_wait_ms: 8}
microburst_mode: off
```
Dan: that's brutal. so continuous batching reduced per-batch similarity? were we grouping by model or by session key?
Alex: batcher was changed to late-bind keying to maximize fill rate: we only assign cohort keys at dispatch. that increased mix of prefixes in batches. result: KV cache sees many cold key accesses instead of contiguous warm accesses.
Sanjay: can you paste a small trace of a request path that missed? curious about keys used.
Alex: pasted a reduced trace (anonymized): 
```
req_id: r-2f3b
seq: [init->user_prompt(prefix: "order_status")]
cache_lookup_keys: ["order_status_v2:user:123", "session:short:xyz"]
backend_calls: [model_variant_a -> kv_miss -> kernel_fwd]
latency_ms: 430
```
Priya: are we seeing this across all model variants or just the transformer-large family?
Alex: biggest impact on opt-family and our 70B derivs (longer KV chains). smaller models less affected.
Maria: quick micro-experiments? rollback the late-bind change on 10% of traffic and compare hit-rate + p95.
Dan: I ran a synthetic workload last night that reproduces the effect locally: enabling late-bind increases hit churn by ~3x. details in my experiment notes.
Sanjay: one thought: maybe we should change cache keying to include a cohort fingerprint that is stable per-session even if batch composition changes. i.e., compute prefix_key earlier (on enqueue) and carry it through dispatch. avoids late-bind mixing.
Alex: yes that's the theory. earlier keying (queue-time keying) would ensure contiguous requests map to same cache keys while still allowing the batcher to mix for GPU efficiency. downside: might reduce batch fill because we reserve affinity.
Priya: tradeoff to quantify: measure delta in avg_batch_size vs hit_rate. we need an expected end-to-end token cost model.
Maria: also check KV warmstart heuristics — currently we evict based on recency globally, not cohort-aware. if we can pin hot cohorts for short windows we'll get better hit-rate without huge memory cost.
Dan: can we add a tiny cohort TTL shadow buffer: on miss, if key belonged to recently seen cohort we prefetch next n tokens into local cache. cheap experiment.
Alex: noted. next steps I propose:
- revert late-bind on 10% (canary) and collect hit_rate/p95 for 24h
- implement queue-time prefix_key as a toggle in batcher (A/B)
- add cohort-aware temporary pin (prefetch on hit) as a low-risk patch
- profiler capture for a sample workload to compare kernel dispatch patterns

Sanjay: +1. I can own the canary revert if infra gives me a window.
Priya: I'll run cost model sims to quantify batch_size vs token cost across hit-rate bands.
Maria: I'll hook up a dashboard with immediate KPIs: prefix_hit_rate, avg_batch_size, p50/p95 latency, tail kernel queue length.
Alex: deploy-bot will do the canary deploy for the revert?
deploy-bot: Canary deploy scheduled: rolling revert of late-bind-keying to 10% of traffic at 1712350800. Monitor channel: #eng-runtime-canaries
Dan: while canary runs i'll attach my reproducer and we can stream perf counters.
Alex: FYI one more datapoint: profiler shows kernel invocation count went up ~20% per request on miss-heavy runs (more small kernel fwd calls rather than long cached kv-resume). so this isn't just cache stat — it increases kernel overhead.
Sanjay: that aligns: KV misses force fresh autoregs and repeated attention compute.
Priya: good to know. if we can get hit_rate back above ~0.45 we should recover most of the latency.
Maria: tagging this thread for postmortem if revert fixes it: we need a clear doc on keying semantics and batcher invariants.
Alex: agreed. I pushed a short runbook to the repo under eng-runtime/ops/warmstart-keying.md and linked it in the canary channel. will share results in ~2h once canary has warm samples. :thumbsup:
